title.narrative: Sahel RESILAND Communal Climate Action and Landscape Management Project

description.narrative: The development objective of Communal Climate Action and Landscape Management Project is to strengthen sustainable landscape management and improve income generation in targeted forest areas in Burkina Faso. This project has four components. The first component, Decentralized management of natural resources, has the following sub-components: Strategic land use planning and management; and : Investments in agro-sylvo-pastoral communal landscapes. The second component, : Institutional strengthening for integrated landscape management, environmental and social risk management, and mobilization of climate finance, has the following sub-components: Intersectoral harmonization, coordination and capacity building for integrated landscape management; Strengthening country systems for environmental and social risk management; and Enabling environment for mobilizing climate finance. The third component, Entrepreneurship and sustainable development of value chains, has the following sub-components: Sustainable development of shea, moringa and other green economy value chains; and Support for cooperatives and SMEs in targeted municipalities. The fourth component, Project coordination, monitoring and evaluation, has the following sub-components: Administration, coordination and project management; and Monitoring and evaluation (M&E), communication and knowledge management.
To strengthen sustainable landscape management and improve income generation in targeted forest areas in Burkina Faso.

condition.narrative: Section I.A.1(a). The Recipient shall maintain at all times during Project implementation, a Project review committee (“ReviewCommittee”) for the Project, with a composition, mandate and resources satisfactory to the Association.

Section I.A.2. The Recipient shall maintain at all times during Project implementation, the Director General of the Green Economyand Climate Change under the MTEE, acting as National Project Coordinator and responsible for Project oversight.

Section I.A.3(d). Not later than thirty (30) days from the Effective Date, or any later date agreed by the Association, theRecipient shall establish and thereafter maintain four (4) regional Project implementation regional branches to support theimplementation and coordination of Project activities in the regions and municipalities selected to participate in the Project, allwith qualifications, experience and terms of reference satisfactory to the Association.

Section I.A.3. (a) The Recipient shall maintain throughout Project implementation a Project implementation unit within the Ministryin charge of environment (“Project Implementation Unit” or “PIU”) with a composition, mandate and resources satisfactory to theAssociation.

Section I.C.1. The Recipient shall prepare and thereafter adopt, not later three (3) months after the Effective Date, or any laterdate as agreed by the Association, a project implementation manual in form and substance satisfactory to the Association.

Section I.G. The Recipient shall, and shall cause the Project Implementing Entity to, ensure that the Project is implemented inaccordance with the Environmental and Social Commitment Plan (“ESCP”), in a manner acceptable to the Association.

Section I.I. Without limitations to Section 5.03 of the General Conditions, the Recipient shall provide, or cause to be provided,promptly as needed, the funds, facilities, services and other resources: (a) required for the Project; and (b) necessary orappropriate to enable the PIU to perform its obligations under the Project.

Section IV. The Recipient shall, not later three (3) months after the Effective Date, or such later date as agreed by theAssociation, customize the accounting software in form and substance satisfactory to the Association.

Within six months of project approval, the Recipient shall carry out a risk assessment of SEA/SH and shall develop, if necessary, aresponse action plan in line with the national provisions and conventions ratified by Burkina Faso.

comment.narrative:
The indicator measures, in hectares, the land area for which new and/or improved sustainable landscape management practices have been introduced. title.narrative: Producers in targeted value chains adopting improved practices across value chains

comment.narrative:
This indicator measures the project's efforts in supporting beneficiaries to adopt improved practices in all targeted value chains. It corresponds to the number of beneficiaries supported in areas related to (i) product certification; (ii) the installation of ridge tops; (iii) acquisition of standards; (iv) certification of shea parks; (v) implementation of PDEs for all types of valuehains; (vi) creation of processing units; (vii) capacity building of beneficiaries (equipment, training, etc.). The indicator corresponds to the PROGREEN indicator ‘Share of land-users adopting new practices in targeted landscapes (%) (disaggregated by poor)' and a target for the PROGREEN source of fund of 10%.
The project estimates that it will reach around 3,200 stakeholders through the financing of value chain sub-projects from the second half of 2024.

During 2024, five (05) new SDADDCs for the communes of Bouroum-Bouroum, Doulougou, Bakata, Sibi and Gomboussougou were drawn up and are awaiting technical validation and adoption by the councils of the special delegations of the communes concerned during the first quarter of 2025.
Due to the non-finalization of the 5 aforementioned SDADDCs, there was an error in the last ISR and the actual value is 5.

title.narrative: Proportion of Communal Development Plans having integrated environment and sustainable development themes

comment.narrative:
The Communal Development Plan (PCD) is the document which determines the main directions and principles of development taking into account the transversal concerns of the municipality on which it bases its investments. This indicator measures the number of PCDs integrating environment and sustainable development themes.
PCDs in updated and adopted in 5 communes (Sapouy, Koumbia, PÃ¢, IpelcA, LAo), with the annual target being 63% achieved. It is anticipated that an additional 5 PCDs will be adopted by November 30, 2025, which will exceed the annual target.

title.narrative: Land charters established on conservation areas

comment.narrative:
This indicator measures the number of conservation areas with a land charter. A land charter is expected to provide a local land agreement inspired by local land customs, uses or practices developed at the local level and aimed at taking into account the diverity of ecological, economic, social and cultural contexts in rural areas.
During 2024, 19 land charters for conservation areas have been drawn up, 7 of which have already been adopted by the special delegations and 29 are under development. The rate of achievement of the annual target (20 charters) is 32% with the 7 charters validated. It is expected that 12 new land charters will be adopted in the first quarter of 2025 by the special delegations. The finalization of the charters was delayed because for quality reasons, the planned PMU involved the General Directorate of Land and Training of the Rural World (DGFOMR) in the analysis of the documents before their adoption by the special delegations of the municipalities.

title.narrative: Proportion of project's physical investments registered in the land cadaster

comment.narrative:
The Project's physical investments is secured when the area is registered in the land cadaster on the basis of the registration (land title). This indicator measures the ratio between the number of registered investments and the total number of project investments.
For the year 2024, the project, in collaboration with the DGI, had planned to register 230 sites, including 45 conservation areas for PDIC/REDD+ in wave 1 communes. By December 31, 2024, 172 sites had been registered, representing a 75% completion rate, achieving the target.
